items.when: The question asks for a percentage of cards in a specific language.

items.statement: The connected table links atoms to bonds via atom_id and bond_id, and does not carry molecule_id for joining atom to bond.
items.when: The query involves the connected table alongside atom and bond.

items.statement: A join between atom and bond must go through the molecule_id column shared by both tables, not through the connected table's bond_id.
items.when: The query needs to relate atoms to bonds in the toxicology schema.

items.statement: Filtering rows to those whose date equals the minimum date in a period returns all tied rows rather than the single earliest record the question requests.
items.when: The question asks for one account or record with the earliest date and multiple rows may share that date.

items.statement: A question asking for the account(s) with the earliest date in a year is answered by ordering the year-filtered rows by date ascending and limiting to one row, not by matching every row whose date equals the minimum date.
items.when: The question asks for the single account or record having the earliest (or latest) date within a specified year.

items.statement: A year-range filter on a date column is expressed as two comparisons on the extracted year, one lower bound and one upper bound.
items.when: The question specifies an inclusive range of years over a date or timestamp column.

items.statement: A SELECT list contains only the columns the question explicitly asks to be returned, not additional identifying columns from joined tables.
items.when: The question asks to calculate or return a specific value without naming an entity column to display alongside it.

items.statement: A query that groups by an entity identifier returns one row per entity, so it cannot produce a per-category aggregate.
items.when: The question asks for counts or ranks per category rather than per entity.

items.statement: When a question asks to rank a category by popularity, the grouping key is the category column, not the individual entity column.
items.when: The question asks for a ranking of a category (such as eye color) by how many entities have it.

items.statement: Joins between cards and foreign_data use cards.uuid = foreign_data.uuid, and table aliases T1/T2 are applied to both tables.
items.when: The question requires combining card attributes with foreign_data attributes.

items.statement: A query that joins cards to foreign_data on uuid and filters foreign_data.language must select cards.name without DISTINCT, because a card's name is unique per uuid and DISTINCT is unnecessary.
items.when: The question asks for card names filtered by a foreign_data language attribute.

items.statement: Peak-month questions over a per-customer monthly table require grouping by the month component and ordering by the aggregate consumption sum, not ordering raw rows.
items.when: The question asks for the month with the highest consumption across multiple customers.

items.statement: When a question asks for a peak month, the result must be the month component of the date column, not the full date value.
items.when: The question asks for a peak or maximum month within a year.

items.statement: A filter on a column of the grouped table belongs in the WHERE clause, not in a set-difference against the unfiltered rows.
items.when: The question restricts the counted set by a value of a column on the primary table while also requiring a HAVING condition on a joined table.

items.statement: Joining races to circuits on circuitId and filtering by circuit name yields one row per race, so duplicate attribute values appear when several races share that attribute.
items.when: The query joins races to circuits and selects a race attribute that is not unique per race.

items.statement: A query that returns a race attribute for races held at a named circuit must return distinct values when the question asks for the set of times rather than one row per race.
items.when: The question asks to list a race attribute for races held at a named circuit and the attribute can repeat across multiple races.

items.statement: A query that filters a child table and returns a parent identifier projects the foreign-key column directly, without DISTINCT, when the question asks which parents satisfy the condition.
items.when: The question asks to identify parent entities by ID based on a property recorded on a child table.

items.statement: Adding DISTINCT to a projection of a foreign-key column that is not unique in the source table silently drops rows that belong to different parent records.
items.when: The question asks for parent IDs reachable through a child table whose join key is not unique per parent, and the projection contains only that key.

items.statement: A question phrased as 'top N teams with the highest X' orders the result by X descending, while 'lowest' or 'bottom' phrasing orders ascending.
items.when: The question specifies a top-N or bottom-N ranking on a numeric attribute.

items.statement: A question asking only for a measured attribute of the top-N teams returns that attribute column alone, without the team name column.
items.when: The question asks for a single measured attribute of the top-N teams and does not ask for team names.

items.statement: Joining a parent table to a child table without DISTINCT returns duplicate values of the parent's attribute when the parent has multiple children.
items.when: The selected column belongs to the table on the one side of a one-to-many join.

items.statement: A query that returns a single attribute from a table joined to another table must use DISTINCT when the join can produce multiple matching rows for one value of that attribute.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute of an entity that is joined to a table with a many-to-one or one-to-many relationship to it.

items.statement: The SELECT list must include every derived column the question asks for, including computed rank columns, in addition to the base columns being ranked.
items.when: The question requests a computed or derived value alongside base columns.

items.statement: A question that asks to rank rows requires a window function such as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ...) in the SELECT list, not merely an ORDER BY clause.
items.when: The question contains a ranking verb (e.g. 'rank') applied to a column.

items.statement: A filter on a boolean column such as isPromo must be applied in the WHERE clause rather than left to the projection.
items.when: The question mentions a promotional printing and the cards table has an isPromo column.

items.statement: When a question asks for the card with the most ruling information, the ranking must count rulings per card rather than aggregate rulings per artist.
items.when: The question asks for a single card with the most ruling information and the schema links rulings to cards by uuid.

items.statement: Counting schools that satisfy a condition uses COUNT over the school code column rather than COUNT(DISTINCT CDSCode).
items.when: The question asks how many schools meet a filter condition.

items.statement: Charter funding type is stored in the frpm table's `Charter Funding Type` column, not in the schools table's FundingType column.
items.when: The question asks about charter funding status or funding type of California schools.

items.statement: A season value in the Match table is a string of the form 'YYYY/YYYY', so a question naming a single calendar year maps to the season string spanning that year and the next.
items.when: The question names a season by a single year and the query filters on Match.season.

items.statement: When a query groups by a team name and orders by an aggregate count, grouping by the team's API id instead of its name prevents distinct teams that share a name from being merged into one group.
items.when: The query aggregates per team and orders by COUNT(*) to pick a single top team.

items.statement: Joining a parent table to a child table on a foreign key and filtering by a child attribute can produce duplicate parent rows, so the projection must be deduplicated when the question targets parent attributes.
items.when: The query selects columns from the parent table while filtering on a column of the child table.

items.statement: A query that returns a column pair from a parent table joined to a child table must use DISTINCT when the question asks for a single location or attribute value rather than one row per child record.
items.when: The question asks for an attribute of an entity that can appear in multiple rows of the joined table, and the expected answer is a single value or a small set of distinct values.

items.statement: Year values are derived by taking the first four characters of the yearmonth Date column with SUBSTRING, since that column stores dates as text.
items.when: The question asks for a year and the relevant date column is yearmonth.Date.

items.statement: Questions about gas consumption are answered from the yearmonth table, whose Consumption column holds gas use, rather than from the transactions_1k table, whose Amount column holds transaction amounts.
items.when: The question asks for the year with the most gas use, or otherwise ranks periods by gas consumption.

items.statement: A query that ranks rows by an aggregate count should order by the count of the join key that links the two tables, not by a different column from the joined table.
items.when: The query joins two tables and orders by COUNT of a column to find the row with the most matches.

items.statement: When a query groups by a column and also selects other columns from the same table, every selected non-aggregated column must appear in the GROUP BY clause.
items.when: The query uses GROUP BY with a mix of aggregated and non-aggregated selected columns.

items.statement: A count of races is computed over races.raceId, not over an unqualified COUNT(*).
items.when: The question asks how many races satisfy a condition.

items.statement: Country filters on the circuits table must list individual country names rather than continent names, because the country column stores countries.
items.when: The question asks to exclude or include races by geographic region such as Asia or Europe.

items.statement: A percentage numerator and denominator must both be computed over the same DISTINCT key set so the ratio is bounded by 100.
items.when: The query computes a percentage as a ratio of two aggregates over a joined result.

items.statement: Joining district on client.district_id and filtering district.A11 to its maximum does not identify the youngest client and can yield zero rows.
items.when: The question asks for the youngest client and the query filters district.A11 against a MAX subquery.

items.statement: A query that must return the single youngest client's account uses a subquery selecting the client_id ordered by birth_date descending with LIMIT 1, rather than comparing birth_date to MAX(birth_date).
items.when: The question asks for accounts of the youngest client and the result must be a single client's accounts.

items.statement: When a date column stores year and month as a six-character string, filtering to a single year uses a prefix match on the first four characters rather than a BETWEEN range over month values.
items.when: The question restricts results to one calendar year and the date column is a YYYYMM string.

items.statement: A query that counts groups satisfying a HAVING condition must wrap the grouped query in a subquery and count its rows, because COUNT with GROUP BY returns one row per group rather than a single total.
items.when: The question asks how many entities satisfy an aggregate condition over grouped rows.

items.statement: Joining circuits to races to results to constructors yields circuit rows rather than the standings positions a position question asks for.
items.when: The question asks for positions rather than circuit names, locations, or countries.

items.statement: Questions asking for positions associated with a constructor are answered from constructorStandings joined to constructors on constructorId, not from circuits or results.
items.when: The question asks for positions and names a constructor.

items.statement: In the card_games schema, the column holding a card's type is named `type`, not `types`.
items.when: The query filters cards by their card type.

items.statement: A query that projects a non-key column from a joined table while filtering on a one-to-many relationship must use DISTINCT to avoid duplicate rows.
items.when: The question asks for a single attribute value (a status, name, or category) rather than a count or aggregate, and the join can produce multiple matching rows per entity.

items.statement: When the question asks for the oldest female client's district, the district is selected by ordering clients with gender 'F' by birth_date ascending and taking the first, rather than by ordering the joined result rows.
items.when: The question asks for accounts of the oldest female client and the query joins client to district.

items.statement: A gap between a district's average salary and the maximum average salary across all districts is computed as the global MAX(A11) minus the global MIN(A11), not as MAX(A11) minus the selected district's A11.
items.when: The question asks for the gap between the lowest average salary and the highest average salary across districts.

items.statement: A query whose question asks which entity ranks highest returns exactly one row when a LIMIT 1 is applied.
items.when: The question asks for the single top-ranked entity and the query uses ORDER BY with LIMIT 1.

items.statement: A query that asks which entity ranks highest returns only the identifying column of that entity, not the aggregate used for ranking.
items.when: The question asks which customer, product, or other entity has the greatest or least value of some measure.

items.statement: Joining Player to Player_Attributes is unnecessary when the requested id and the ordering attribute both reside in Player_Attributes.
items.when: The question asks for an id and an ordering attribute that are both columns of Player_Attributes.

items.statement: When a question asks for a player id and the ranking attribute lives in Player_Attributes, the id column is Player_Attributes.id rather than Player.player_api_id.
items.when: The question requests a player id and the ordering attribute is a column of Player_Attributes.

items.statement: Joining races to circuits and filtering on circuit country without DISTINCT can return duplicate race names when a race is associated with multiple matching circuit rows.
items.when: The question asks for race names and the filter is on a circuit column rather than a race column.

items.statement: A query that asks for the name of a race held on circuits in a country must return each race name at most once, so DISTINCT is required when the join can multiply rows.
items.when: The question asks for race names filtered by a circuit attribute such as country.

items.statement: A join between cards and legalities on uuid can produce duplicate card rows, so DISTINCT is applied when the question asks for a list of cards.
items.when: The query joins cards to legalities and the question asks for a list of cards.

items.statement: String literals compared against a column must match the stored casing of that column's values.
items.when: A filter compares a text column to a literal value whose casing differs from the data.

items.statement: Counting rows that satisfy a filter uses COUNT on the key column without DISTINCT when the join is many-to-one from the counted table to the joined table.
items.when: The question asks how many entities of one table meet conditions, and the join to the other table is on that table's foreign key.

items.statement: A filter on a column of one table must reference that table's alias, not another joined table's alias.
items.when: The query joins two tables and a WHERE predicate names a column that exists in only one of them.

items.statement: Applying DISTINCT to a column that is not unique per entity in the joined result can drop rows that belong to distinct entities sharing that value.
items.when: The question asks for a list of attribute values and the selected attribute may repeat across distinct matching entities.

items.statement: A ratio expression must not be wrapped in a CAST to REAL when the numerator already uses a decimal literal such as 1.0 to force floating-point division.
items.when: The SQL computes a ratio using SUM(CASE ...) over two groups.

items.statement: When a question asks for a ratio of A to B, the numerator must count A and the denominator must count B in the order named by the question.
items.when: The question asks for a ratio of one named group to another named group.

items.statement: An inclusive range condition on overall_rating is expressed with BETWEEN using the two stated bounds.
items.when: The question gives an overall rating range with both endpoints stated as inclusive.

items.statement: A count of players filtered only by attributes stored in Player_Attributes is computed from Player_Attributes alone, without joining Player.
items.when: The question asks for a count of players whose only stated conditions are columns of Player_Attributes.

items.statement: When a question names a single entity by a unique name, the filter on that name belongs on the entity's own table and the join is used only to reach the requested column.
items.when: The question identifies one row by a name column and asks for a column stored on a related table.

items.statement: A query that asks where a single named entity's attribute can be found returns one row per matching entity, so duplicate rows from a one-to-many join must be removed with DISTINCT.
items.when: The question asks for a location or URL of one named entity and the join path from that entity to the requested column is one-to-many.

items.statement: When a query groups by a unique id plus a display column but selects only the display column, grouping by the display column alone yields the deduplicated result.
items.when: The selected column is functionally determined by the grouping column and duplicates appear in the output.

items.statement: Grouping by a unique identifier column in addition to the selected display column can produce duplicate display values when the identifier is not selected.
items.when: The query groups by both a unique id column and a name column while selecting only the name.

items.statement: A query that ranks customers by an aggregate over a period must group by the customer identifier and order by the aggregate expression, not by a single row's value.
items.when: The question asks for a customer ranked by a summed or averaged measure across multiple rows.

items.statement: When a question asks for the customer with the least or most total consumption over a period, consumption must be aggregated per customer before ordering.
items.when: The question asks for a customer ranked by least or most consumption over a time period, and the consumption table has multiple rows per customer.

items.statement: Filtering a department column with a value that omits the stored suffix returns no rows.

items.statement: Department values stored in the major table include the word 'Department' as a suffix, so filters on department must match the stored literal exactly.
items.when: The query filters rows by a department name in the student_club schema.

items.statement: A WHERE column = (SELECT MAX(column) ...) pattern returns multiple rows when the maximum value is shared, so it does not satisfy questions that ask for a single top-ranked item.
items.when: The question requests one item and the target column may contain duplicate maximum values.

items.statement: Questions asking for the single card with the highest value of a numeric column require a query that returns exactly one row, such as ORDER BY that column DESC with LIMIT 1, rather than a WHERE equality against a MAX subquery that can match ties.

items.statement: A subquery that computes per-molecule counts and is then averaged must group by molecule_id and expose a single count column for the outer AVG.
items.when: The question asks for an average of a per-entity count rather than a count of rows.

items.statement: When counting atoms of a given element per molecule, joining atom and bond directly on molecule_id and filtering bond_type in the WHERE clause yields the same per-molecule counts as joining through the molecule table.
items.when: The question asks for an average or aggregate over per-molecule counts of atoms of a specific element, and the schema links atom and bond via molecule_id.

items.statement: Returning one row per candidate value with ORDER BY and LIMIT 1 answers a ranking question, not a which-is-higher question.
items.when: the question asks which of two values is higher and the answer must name one of them

items.statement: Questions asking which of two values is higher require a single comparison result rather than a row per candidate value.
items.when: the question asks which of two aggregates is higher

items.statement: Selecting the top row by a numeric column is expressed with ORDER BY that column DESC plus LIMIT 1 rather than a MAX subquery in the WHERE clause.
items.when: The question asks for the row holding the maximum value of a column and the schema supports ORDER BY with LIMIT.

items.statement: A query that answers a question asking for a single attribute returns only that attribute, not additional columns used to filter or order.
items.when: The question names exactly one attribute to report (e.g., a name) and other columns appear only in filtering or ordering logic.

items.statement: Queries that join qualifying to drivers on driverId and select the driver surname for a given raceId use table aliases and an INNER JOIN.
items.when: The question asks for a driver surname based on a qualifying result in a specific race.

items.statement: Filtering out NULL values in a qualifying-time column before ordering by that column is redundant when the query selects the minimum non-null value via ascending order and LIMIT 1, because NULLs sort last in ascending order in the target dialect.
items.when: The question asks for the driver with the best (minimum) lap time in a qualifying period and the query orders ascending by that time column with LIMIT 1.

items.statement: Negating a conjunction with NOT (A IS NOT NULL AND B IS NOT NULL) is not equivalent to requiring both A and B to be null.

items.statement: A card is excluded from the set of borderless cards without powerful foils only when both cardKingdomFoilId and cardKingdomId are non-null.

items.statement: A rate computed as a ratio of two columns is filtered for non-null results by testing the ratio expression itself with IS NOT NULL rather than by requiring the denominator to be greater than zero.

items.statement: Continuation-school status is recorded in the frpm table's `Educational Option Type` column, not in the schools table's DOC column.
items.when: The question filters schools by continuation-school status.

items.statement: Joining transactions_1k and products to answer a question about gas-station attributes produces an incorrect result because those joins are unnecessary.
items.when: The question's filter and output columns all belong to the gasstations table.

items.statement: Gas-station attributes such as Country and Segment are columns of the gasstations table and are filtered there without joining transactions or products.
items.when: The question asks for a count or property of gas stations filtered by a station attribute like country or segment.

items.statement: Integer division in a percentage computation is avoided by casting one operand to a real or floating type before dividing.
items.when: The percentage is computed from two integer-valued SUM or COUNT expressions.

items.statement: A question asking for a single derived ratio or percentage is answered by one projected expression, not by also projecting the numerator and denominator as separate columns.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage or ratio deviation and does not separately ask for the underlying counts.

items.statement: Eliminated-in-Q1 queries are answered by ordering qualifying rows by q1 descending and limiting to the number of elimination slots, rather than by matching a single aggregate value.
items.when: The question asks which drivers were eliminated in the first qualifying period.

items.statement: Questions asking for drivers eliminated in the first qualifying period require selecting the bottom-ranked drivers by q1 time, not the single driver with the maximum q1 time.
items.when: The question asks for drivers eliminated in the first qualifying period of a race.

items.statement: When a question asks which entity has the maximum value and ties are possible, the query must return all entities tied at the maximum rather than a single row via ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1.
items.when: The question asks which entity has the highest value on an attribute.

items.statement: A comparison question asking which of two named entities has a higher value requires returning only the identifier of the winner, not the compared value itself.
items.when: The question asks which of two named entities has a higher value on some attribute.

items.statement: A filter on a nullable foreign-key column is paired with a non-null check on the companion foreign-key column when the question implies both references must be present.
items.when: The question describes entities that have a specific linked attribute and the schema exposes two related foreign-key columns on the same table.

items.statement: Questions asking which entities have a property are answered by selecting the entity's identifier column, not a descriptive name column.
items.when: The question asks which rows satisfy a condition rather than asking for a name or description of those rows.

items.statement: String literal values compared against a column must match the stored casing exactly, so a value written with different capitalization than the data returns no rows.
items.when: A WHERE clause compares a text column to a literal whose capitalization differs from the stored value.

items.statement: Counting rows that satisfy a filter uses COUNT(column) rather than COUNT(DISTINCT column) when the join key is unique per row of the counted table.
items.when: The question asks how many rows of one table match a filter and the query joins that table to another on a key that is unique in the counted table.

items.statement: A query answering a who-is question returns only the columns naming the person, excluding columns that merely support filtering or ordering.
items.when: The question asks 'who' and the supporting column is not itself requested.

items.statement: A query that asks who is the youngest or oldest among a set of people returns only identifying name columns, not the birth-date column used for ordering.
items.when: The question asks for a superlative person (youngest/oldest) and the answer is ordered by a date-of-birth column.

items.statement: When a question asks for a percentage, the denominator counts the rows of the population being described, so a filter restricting that population must be applied to the denominator as well as the numerator.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage and the SQL includes a WHERE clause restricting the population.

items.statement: A percentage over a filtered subset of rows is computed as the count of rows matching the condition divided by the count of rows in the filtered subset, not by the count of all rows in the table.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of rows satisfying a condition among a subset defined by a WHERE filter.

items.statement: Integer division of two count columns must be cast to a real type before dividing to produce a fractional rate.
items.when: The requested rate is computed by dividing one integer count column by another integer count column.

items.statement: A query that asks for a single computed rate returns only that computed expression, not the source columns used to derive it.
items.when: The question asks for a rate or ratio value rather than the underlying counts or names.

items.statement: Applying strftime to a transaction Date column to match a month string yields no rows when the schema's month information is stored in a separate yearmonth table keyed by CustomerID.
items.when: The query filters transactions by month using a date-format function on the transaction date column while a yearmonth table exists in the schema.

items.statement: When a schema contains a precomputed yearmonth table keyed by CustomerID and Date, filtering transactions by month requires joining transactions to yearmonth on CustomerID and filtering on yearmonth.Date rather than applying a date function to the transaction date column.
items.when: The question asks for products or transactions restricted to a specific month and the schema includes a yearmonth table with CustomerID and Date columns.

items.statement: Joining expense to budget and event to reach category and date columns yields no rows when the expense table already stores the description and date directly.
items.when: The question names an expense description and a date, and the expense table has expense_description and expense_date columns.

items.statement: Expense records carry their own description and date columns, so filtering expenses by description and date requires no join to budget or event.
items.when: The question asks for expense amounts filtered by a description or date that exists as a column on the expense table.

items.statement: Filtering a parent table by patient attributes and then joining to a child table is equivalent to selecting from the child table with an ID IN subquery over the parent table.
items.when: The query joins Patient to Examination on ID and filters on Patient columns.

items.statement: Questions asking for a patient's antibody concentration status require all antibody measurement columns (aCL IgA, aCL IgG, aCL IgM) to be selected, not just one of them.
items.when: The question asks for anti-Cardiolipin antibody concentration status or similar multi-component lab status for a patient.

items.statement: Filtering status text with NOT LIKE 'Finished%' and NOT LIKE '+%' does not correctly capture non-finishing drivers.
items.when: The question asks for drivers who did not finish and the query filters on the status table's status column.

items.statement: A driver who did not finish a race is identified by a null results.time value rather than by the status text.
items.when: The question asks how many drivers did not finish a race.

items.statement: Joining a parent table to a child table is unnecessary when the requested output column and the filter column both live in the child table.
items.when: The question asks for a column that exists in the same table as the column being filtered.

items.statement: Filter values for a categorical column must match the stored representation exactly, including surrounding whitespace.
items.when: The query filters on a categorical column whose stored values may contain padding or whitespace.

items.statement: A GROUP BY query whose ORDER BY uses an aggregate must order by that aggregate expression rather than by a select-list alias when the alias is not projected.
items.when: The select list omits the aggregate that the ordering depends on.

items.statement: A query that asks which entities have a top-N ranking by an aggregate returns only the entity column, not the aggregate value.
items.when: The question asks which groups have the top or bottom N by some aggregate rather than asking for the aggregate value itself.

items.statement: A query that returns a per-customer aggregate ranked to a single top row must group by the customer identifier and order by the aggregate with a limit of one.
items.when: The question asks for the top customer by an aggregate of consumption.

items.statement: When a question asks for the biggest monthly consumption of a group of customers, the answer is the maximum over customers of each customer's average monthly consumption, not the maximum of any single month's consumption.
items.when: The question asks for a per-customer monthly consumption aggregate (such as biggest monthly consumption) for a filtered set of customers.

items.statement: Ordering by a nullable date column without filtering out NULLs can place NULL rows first and yield an empty or wrong result.
items.when: The ORDER BY column can contain NULL values and the query uses LIMIT to pick the earliest row.

items.statement: A question asking for the first patient with a given diagnosis is answered from the Patient table's own diagnosis and first-date columns, not by joining to an examination table.
items.when: The question asks for a patient attribute for the earliest patient with a specified diagnosis.

items.statement: A date stored as a text column is filtered by year with SUBSTR(Date,1,4) and grouped by month with SUBSTR(Date,5,2).
items.when: The date column is textual in YYYYMM form and the question constrains by year while aggregating per month.

items.statement: Questions asking for the highest monthly aggregate require grouping by month and ordering by the aggregate, not applying MAX directly to the value column.
items.when: The question asks for the highest or lowest value of a per-month aggregate over a date range.

items.statement: A computed CASE expression is left unaliased so the result column name is the CASE expression itself rather than a generic alias such as 'Answer'.
items.when: The query's only output column is a CASE expression and the question does not name a required output column.

items.statement: A CASE expression that answers a yes/no question about a laboratory value uses the value labels 'Normal' and 'Abnormal' rather than 'Yes' and 'No'.
items.when: The question asks whether a laboratory measurement is at a normal level and the answer is produced by a CASE expression over that measurement.

items.statement: When a question asks for a single entity attribute, the SELECT list contains only the column holding that attribute rather than every column describing the relationship row.
items.when: The question names one attribute to return and the matching table row contains additional columns beyond that attribute.

items.statement: A query asking for the atom IDs of a bond returns only the atom_id column, not both atom_id and atom_id2.
items.when: The question asks for the atom IDs of a specific bond identified by bond_id.

items.statement: A comparison against an aggregate over a filtered subset is computed by a subquery that repeats the same join and filter as the outer query.
items.when: The question asks for rows whose value exceeds an average computed over the same population the outer query draws from.

items.statement: The column holding a school's document type is named DOC in the schools table, not DOCType.
items.when: The question asks for a school's DOC type or document type and the query selects from the schools table.

items.statement: Filtering a date column by year requires extracting the year from the column rather than comparing the raw date to a year boundary string.
items.when: The question specifies a year threshold and the column stores full dates.

items.statement: A question that asks to list a value only if there is any requires a LEFT JOIN from the primary table to the optional table, not an inner join.
items.when: The question asks for a column from a related table qualified by a phrase such as 'if there is any' or 'if available'.

items.statement: Grouping by a customer identifier while selecting a segment column returns one row per customer rather than one row per segment.
items.when: The SELECT list contains a segment column and the GROUP BY clause contains a customer identifier.

items.statement: A query that asks which segment has the least or most of an aggregated measure groups by the segment column, not by the entity identifier.
items.when: The question asks for a segment-level ranking by an aggregate such as total consumption.

items.statement: A question asking whether each item was approved requires the approval status column to be selected, not the item identifier or description.
items.when: The question asks about the approval status of each record.

items.statement: Date equality filters on a datetime column can miss rows whose stored value includes a time component, so a prefix match is needed to capture all rows on that calendar date.
items.when: The question specifies a calendar date and the filtered column stores datetime values rather than pure dates.

items.statement: Selecting the row with the highest value in a column is expressed by ordering on that column descending and limiting to one row.
items.when: The question asks for the record associated with the maximum value of a column.

items.statement: A LIKE pattern built from a user-supplied lap time must match the stored textual format of the time column, including whether minutes are zero-padded.
items.when: A query filters a time column using a LIKE pattern derived from a time value stated in the question.

items.statement: Q3 lap times in the qualifying table are stored in minute:second.millisecond format without a leading zero on the minutes component, so a time of 0:01:33 is stored as '1:33...'.
items.when: The question supplies a qualifying lap time with a leading zero on the minutes and the query filters the q3 column with a LIKE pattern.

items.statement: Joining cards to rulings on uuid and selecting rulings.text yields no rows for a card that has legality formats but no rulings.
items.when: The question concerns a card's play legality rather than its rulings text.

items.statement: Joining a connectivity table to an atom table and unioning the two endpoint columns yields one row per atom rather than a single row pairing the two bonded atoms.
items.when: The question expects a single row describing a bond's two endpoints.

items.statement: A question asking for the atoms bonded by a specific bond requires returning the two atom identifiers encoded in that bond's bond_id, not the rows of a connectivity table joined to an atom table.
items.when: The question names a specific bond and asks which atoms it bonds.

items.statement: A meal-count threshold in a California schools question is matched against the Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17) column, not the FRPM Count (Ages 5-17) column.
items.when: The question asks for schools exceeding a numeric threshold on free or reduced-price meals.

items.statement: A city name in a California schools question is matched against the County column, not the City column, when the question refers to a county-level region.
items.when: The question names a place that could be either a city or a county and the schema has both City and County columns.

items.statement: An age computed as a fixed reference year minus a birth year is expressed as a numeric subtraction, not a string subtraction.
items.when: The question asks for an average age as of a stated year derived from a birthday column.

items.statement: A date range that names a month covers the first day through the last day of that month, inclusive.
items.when: The question specifies a month and year for a date filter.

items.statement: When a question asks for one attribute of a named entity, the query joins the entity table to the attribute table on the shared entity key and filters by the entity name, projecting only the requested attribute.
items.when: The question names a specific entity and asks for one of its attributes stored in a separate table.

items.statement: A query that asks for a single attribute value of a named entity must return at most one row, so a DISTINCT or equivalent deduplication is required when the joined attribute table can contain multiple rows per entity.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute value of a single named entity and the attribute is stored in a table that may have multiple rows per entity key.

items.statement: A query that returns the nationality of drivers matching a qualifying condition must use DISTINCT when multiple qualifying rows can join to the same driver.
items.when: The question asks for a driver attribute and the join path goes through qualifying, which can contain several rows per driver.

items.statement: Lap-time values stored in qualifying.q2 are formatted without a leading zero on the minutes component, so a time written as 0:01:15 in a question corresponds to a stored value beginning with 1:15.
items.when: The question specifies a qualifying lap time and the answer depends on matching that time against the q2 column.

items.statement: Queries that look up a single attribute of one named entity use DISTINCT when the join to a related table can multiply rows.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute of a single named entity and the answer is joined to a table that may have multiple rows per entity.

items.statement: A query that returns the type of a named card must join cards to foreign_data on uuid so that only cards with foreign-language printings are matched.
items.when: The question asks for an attribute of a specific named card and the schema contains a foreign_data table keyed by uuid.

items.statement: Percentage calculations over gas stations divide by COUNT(GasStationID) rather than COUNT(*).
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of gas stations matching a condition.

items.statement: When a question attributes a patient-level attribute to examination records, the attribute is retrieved by joining Examination to Patient on the shared ID column.
items.when: The question references a patient attribute (such as diagnosis) while filtering on examination fields like Examination Date.

items.statement: Diagnosis values are stored on the Patient table, not on the Examination table, so queries that group or select a diagnosis must join Examination to Patient on ID.
items.when: The question asks for a diagnosis or illness associated with examination records.

items.statement: Date-part filters on a stored date string can be expressed as a single prefix comparison against the concatenated year and month.
items.when: The birthday column stores dates as text in YYYY-MM-DD form and the question constrains both year and month.

items.statement: A query that asks only for a list of named entities returns just the requested identifying column, not all columns of the source table.
items.when: The question names a single attribute to list (such as player names) rather than asking for full records.

items.statement: Counting a non-null foreign key column in a joined table yields the same aggregate as counting the joined table's primary key when the foreign key is non-null for every matching row.
items.when: The query counts rows of a joined table via a foreign key column that is non-null on every matched row.

items.statement: When a query groups by a table's primary key and also selects another column from that table, grouping by the primary key alone is sufficient because the other column is functionally dependent on it.
items.when: The query groups by a table's primary key and selects additional columns from the same table.

items.statement: A threshold stated as 'greater than or equal to N' is expressed with >= N, not > N.
items.when: The question specifies an inclusive lower bound on a numeric column.

items.statement: Integer division of two integer columns yields 0 for any ratio below 1, so a ratio comparison against a decimal threshold requires casting the numerator to REAL.
items.when: A WHERE clause divides one integer column by another and compares the result to a fractional threshold.

items.statement: Queries that join two tables on a shared key alias both tables and qualify every column reference with its alias.
items.when: The query joins two or more tables and references columns from more than one of them.

items.statement: String comparisons against a column whose stored values are capitalized must use the capitalized form of the literal.
items.when: The query filters a text column on a literal value and the schema's stored values for that column are capitalized.

items.statement: Excluding entities that have a related row with a given attribute value is expressed as a NOT EXISTS subquery or an anti-join on the related table, not as a filter on the entity table alone.
items.when: The question asks for entities that do not contain a related attribute, and the attribute lives in a child table joined by a foreign key.

items.statement: A percentage whose denominator counts rows of a filtered base table must use the same filter in the numerator's population, not a narrower subset condition.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of a labeled subset of entities and the numerator applies an additional per-entity property condition.

items.statement: Restricting a connectivity query to the neighbor atom alone omits the molecule's own atoms and undercounts the connected set.
items.when: The query joins a connectivity table to an atom table filtered by molecule_id and projects only the neighbor-side atom_id.

items.statement: A question asking for atoms connected to a molecule's atoms requires returning both endpoints of each connected edge, not only the atom on the far side of the edge.
items.when: The question asks for atoms connected to the atoms of a specified molecule and the connected table stores atom pairs.

items.statement: A join between schools and satscores on CDSCode = cds can silently drop rows when the two tables do not share matching codes, so a query returning no rows may indicate a join-key mismatch rather than an empty result set.
items.when: A query joining schools to satscores on CDSCode = cds returns zero rows.

items.statement: The satscores table already carries the county name in its cname column, so county-filtered school queries can be answered from satscores alone without joining schools.
items.when: The question asks for a school attribute filtered by county and the needed attribute is present in satscores.

items.statement: Joining transactions_1k and products to gasstations to count gas stations by segment yields no rows when the segment label lives on the gasstations table rather than on product descriptions.
items.when: The question's filter value is a segment label that appears as a column on the gasstations table.

items.statement: A question asking which country has the most gas stations of a given segment is answered from the gasstations table alone, filtering on its Segment column and grouping by Country.
items.when: The question asks for a country ranking by count of gas stations of a described segment.

items.statement: When a question asks for patients who had not undergone an examination until at least a year after their first visit, the query must count patients whose earliest examination date is at least one year after First Date, not patients having any examination at least a year later.
items.when: The question asks about patients who had not undergone an examination until at least a year following their initial visit.

items.statement: A filter on a patient attribute such as Admission belongs in the WHERE clause of the query that counts patients, not only in the join condition.
items.when: The question restricts which patients are counted by a value stored on the Patient table.

items.statement: An average over a column is computed as the sum of that column divided by the count of rows in the filtered set, not by averaging a differently filtered subset.
items.when: The question asks for a comparison against an average over the same filtered population.

items.statement: A year filter on a datetime column must match the whole year, not a single month within it.
items.when: The question names a year and the date column stores full timestamps.

items.statement: Queries that join two tables alias each table and qualify every column reference with its alias.
items.when: The query involves a join between two or more tables.

items.statement: String comparisons against enumerated status values are case-sensitive in the target dialect, so the literal must match the stored casing exactly.
items.when: A filter compares a text column against a literal value drawn from an enumerated set.

items.statement: Joining transactions directly to dispositions without routing through the account table produces a cross-product that inflates row counts.
items.when: The query relates transaction attributes to disposition attributes.

items.statement: A transaction-to-disposition join must traverse the account table, since transactions and dispositions share no direct key.
items.when: The question asks for a disposition attribute of a client identified by transaction attributes.

items.statement: Questions asking who achieved something in a race require selecting driver identity columns (forename, surname, url) rather than only the driver url.
items.when: The question asks for a person's identity or profile link and the answer joins drivers to lapTimes.

items.statement: Lap time values in the formula_1 database are stored without a leading zero before the minutes component, so a time of 0:01:27 is stored as 1:27.
items.when: The question specifies a lap time with a leading zero in the minutes component and the query filters lapTimes.time.

items.statement: Joining a card table to a set-translation table on a key that is not the card's set foreign key produces duplicate rows and overcounts distinct values.
items.when: The query joins cards to set_translations and the join predicate does not use the card's set identifier.

items.statement: When a question asks for a property of the set that a named card belongs to, the query must resolve the card to its set and then read the property from that set's row, not join through unrelated keys that multiply rows.
items.when: The question names a specific card and asks for an attribute of the set containing it.

items.statement: Per-category counts over a shared join are produced by wrapping each category predicate in a CASE expression inside COUNT(DISTINCT ...), with NULL for non-matching rows.
items.when: The question requests separate counts for multiple values of the same column under identical join and filter conditions.

items.statement: A question asking for counts of two distinct element categories requires one separate aggregate column per category rather than a single combined count.
items.when: The question asks how many atoms of two different element types satisfy a shared join and filter condition.

items.statement: Columns used in ORDER BY or in arithmetic expressions should be guarded with an IS NOT NULL filter when nulls would corrupt the ordering or the computed value.
items.when: The query orders by or computes from a column that may contain nulls.

items.statement: When a question asks for a value used to order or select rows (such as the patient's birthday used to find the oldest patient), that value must also appear in the SELECT list.
items.when: The question asks for an attribute of the row chosen by an ORDER BY or LIMIT criterion.

items.statement: Rows with a NULL value in the column used for ordering are excluded when the query selects the minimum or maximum by that column.
items.when: The ORDER BY column used to pick an extreme value is nullable in the schema.

items.statement: A query that asks who is the oldest or youngest among a set of entities returns only the identifying columns named by the question, not the ordering column used to determine the extreme.
items.when: The question asks for a person or entity by a superlative such as oldest or youngest and does not explicitly request the attribute used for comparison.

items.statement: Filtering records to a single calendar year uses a year-extraction function on the date column compared to the year string, rather than a BETWEEN range over full dates.
items.when: The question names a specific year and the date column stores full dates.

items.statement: A monthly average over a calendar year is computed as a real division of the year's count by 12, with the count cast to a real type rather than relying on a decimal literal divisor.
items.when: The question asks for an average per month over a year of records.

items.statement: Selecting an attribute without DISTINCT can return multiple rows when the same entity name matches several records with differing values in other columns.
items.when: The filter predicate matches multiple rows that share the requested attribute value.

items.statement: A query that asks for a single attribute value of a named entity must return at most one row, so DISTINCT or an equivalent uniqueness guarantee is required when the attribute may repeat across matching rows.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute value of a specific named entity and the attribute column is not guaranteed unique per entity.

items.statement: Filtering rows with a WHERE clause on a subquery MAX value does not by itself select the oldest client within the top branch when multiple clients share that branch.
items.when: The question requires both a branch-level extremum and a client-level ordering within that branch.

items.statement: A question asking for an attribute of the oldest client in the highest-average-salary branch requires ordering by the branch's average salary descending first, then by birth date ascending, and taking the first row.
items.when: The question asks for an attribute of the oldest client associated with the branch having the maximum average salary.

items.statement: The value 'Directly funded' in the Charter Funding Type column corresponds to the phrase 'directly funded' in questions.
items.when: A question mentions directly funded schools and the query involves the frpm table's Charter Funding Type column.

items.statement: Races are joined to seasons on the year column shared by both tables.
items.when: The question requires season attributes for a specific race.

items.statement: A query that asks only for a season page URL returns the url column alone, not the year column used to join races to seasons.
items.when: The question asks for a season page or season URL for a race, without also asking for the year itself.

items.statement: Adding LIMIT 1 to a query whose answer is a set of values silently drops rows and undercounts the result.
items.when: The question requests all values of a column for a named entity rather than a single representative value.

items.statement: A LIMIT clause is omitted when the question asks what values a column holds for a named entity, because the answer is the full set of matching rows rather than a single row.
items.when: The question asks for the value(s) of a column for a named entity and does not ask for a single or top result.

items.statement: When a question asks to show a stored score column alongside a ranking, the score column is selected directly rather than aggregated with AVG.
items.when: The question names a specific score column and asks for ranking by that score.

items.statement: A question that asks to rank rows requires a rank or row-number column in the result, not merely an ORDER BY clause.
items.when: The question contains a ranking verb such as rank or top-N and the expected output includes a rank column.

items.statement: When the requested output is a count difference, the result column must be the difference of counts rather than a difference of summed amounts.
items.when: The question asks 'how many more' of one category than another.

items.statement: A question asking how many more of one group than another requires counting rows per group, not summing a monetary amount column.
items.when: The question compares counts of entities between two categories and asks for the difference.

items.statement: When a query joins a team table to a per-team attribute table and selects team names, duplicate team names can appear unless DISTINCT is applied or the join is guaranteed one-to-one.
items.when: The query selects team names from a join between a team table and a per-team attribute table.

items.statement: Averages over a column that may contain NULLs must exclude NULL rows from both the numerator and the denominator, since AVG ignores NULLs but SUM/COUNT does not.
items.when: The query computes an average of a nullable column, especially via SUM/COUNT rather than AVG.

items.statement: Selecting both columns of a connection table answers a question about which pairs are connected, not a question about which entities are connected.
items.when: The question asks which entities are connected rather than which pairs of entities are connected.

items.statement: A query that asks which entities are connected returns each qualifying entity once, so duplicate rows from a connection table must be eliminated with DISTINCT.
items.when: The question asks which entities are connected and the answer is drawn from a table that stores pairs of connected entities.

items.statement: A driver's number is retrieved by joining qualifying to drivers on driverId, since the number column lives in the drivers table and not in qualifying.
items.when: The question asks for a driver's number and the filter condition is on a qualifying column.

items.statement: A qualifying time stored in a q1/q2/q3 column is matched with a LIKE prefix pattern on the minute:second portion rather than an equality comparison against a full time string.
items.when: The question supplies a qualifying lap time and the answer depends on matching rows in a qualifying time column.

items.statement: A query listing users who own qualifying posts must return one row per qualifying post-owner pairing rather than deduplicating by display name, so the result count matches the number of qualifying posts.
items.when: The question asks to list display names of users who own a post satisfying a predicate.

items.statement: Adding DISTINCT to a query that joins users to posts on OwnerUserId can drop rows when a user owns multiple qualifying posts, because DISTINCT collapses duplicate display names.
items.when: The question asks for display names of users who own at least one post matching a condition, and the join is users-to-posts on OwnerUserId.

items.statement: Selecting a column without DISTINCT from a table where the filter matches multiple rows yields duplicate values rather than the single value the question requests.
items.when: The filter predicate matches more than one row but the question asks for one value.

items.statement: A query that returns a single attribute for a named entity must use DISTINCT when the underlying table can hold multiple rows per entity, so that duplicate values collapse to one row.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute value of a specific named entity and the answer is expected to be a single value.

items.statement: Joining the atom table to connected and selecting only atom.atom_id loses the second atom of each connected pair.
items.when: The connected table represents a pair of atoms and the question asks which atoms are connected.

items.statement: Questions asking which atoms are connected by a bond type require returning both atom columns from the connected table, not a single atom_id.
items.when: The question asks what atoms are connected by a given bond type and the connected table holds two atom columns.

items.statement: Ordering by a per-row score column without grouping by the entity being ranked produces a different district than aggregating the score by that entity.
items.when: The question asks which group has the highest average of a column that appears on multiple rows per group.

items.statement: When a question asks for the district with the highest average reading score among active schools, the query must aggregate the reading score by district rather than order by a single row's score.
items.when: The question asks for a district-level ranking based on an average score across schools.

items.statement: Filtering rows by equality to a subquery MAX value returns every row tied at that maximum, so it does not satisfy a request for a single top-ranked entity.
items.when: The question asks for one player with the highest rating and multiple rows share the maximum value.

items.statement: A query asking for the single player with the highest value of a column must return exactly one row, which requires ORDER BY on that column with LIMIT 1 rather than an equality filter against the maximum value.

items.statement: Matching a qualifying lap time from a question requires a pattern comparison (LIKE with a wildcard) rather than exact string equality.
items.when: The question asks for rows whose qualifying time column equals a time value stated in the question.

items.statement: Values in the q2 column of the qualifying table are stored in a format that does not match the m:ss or h:mm:ss literal shown in the question, so equality against the question's literal returns no rows.
items.when: The question supplies a lap time literal for a qualifying time column and the answer must match rows in that column.

items.statement: A query that returns zero rows cannot be the correct answer when the question presupposes at least one matching record exists.
items.when: The candidate SQL returns an empty result set for a question whose phrasing implies a non-empty answer.

items.statement: Joining expense to budget and event and filtering on event.type yields no rows when the expense rows' link_to_budget values do not match any budget row, so the join chain silently drops all candidates.

items.statement: Joining races and circuits to obtain a constructor's country yields the circuit's country rather than the constructor's country.

items.statement: A constructor's country is stored in the constructors table's nationality column, not in the circuits table's country column.

items.statement: When a percentage is requested, the denominator counts rows of the entity being measured (cards.id), not rows of the attribute table.
items.when: The question asks for a percentage of an entity whose attribute is stored in a joined table.

items.statement: A percentage of cards in a given language must be computed over the cards table joined to foreign_data on uuid, not over foreign_data alone.

items.statement: The connected table links atoms to bonds via atom_id and bond_id, and does not carry molecule_id for joining atom to bond.

items.statement: A join between atom and bond must go through the molecule_id column shared by both tables, not through the connected table's bond_id.
items.when: The query needs to relate atoms to bonds in the toxicology schema.

items.statement: Filtering rows to those whose date equals the minimum date in a period returns all tied rows rather than the single earliest record the question requests.

items.when: The question asks for the single account or record having the earliest (or latest) date within a specified year.

items.statement: Filtering rows to those equal to a global minimum before averaging yields a different result than averaging all rows in each group.
items.when: The query computes an average per group and the question references a minimum consumption value.

items.statement: When a question asks for the difference between group averages, the average is computed over all rows in each group, not only over rows that attain the group minimum.
items.when: The question asks for a difference in averages between groups and also mentions a least or minimum amount.

items.statement: Using COUNT(DISTINCT id) over a join as the numerator while dividing by a scalar subquery that counts all rows of the base table produces a ratio whose numerator and denominator cover different populations.

items.statement: A percentage of a subpopulation that is defined by a filter on the same table as the numerator must use the filtered row count as the denominator, not the unfiltered table count.

items.statement: A year-range filter on a date column is expressed as two comparisons on the extracted year, one lower bound and one upper bound.
items.when: The question specifies an inclusive range of years over a date or timestamp column.

items.statement: A SELECT list contains only the columns the question explicitly asks to be returned, not additional identifying columns from joined tables.
items.when: The question asks to calculate or return a specific value without naming an entity column to display alongside it.

items.statement: Joins between cards and foreign_data use cards.uuid = foreign_data.uuid, and table aliases T1/T2 are applied to both tables.

items.statement: A query that joins cards to foreign_data on uuid and filters foreign_data.language must select cards.name without DISTINCT, because a card's name is unique per uuid and DISTINCT is unnecessary.

items.statement: Peak-month questions over a per-customer monthly table require grouping by the month component and ordering by the aggregate consumption sum, not ordering raw rows.

items.statement: When a question asks for a peak month, the result must be the month component of the date column, not the full date value.
items.when: The question asks for a peak or maximum month within a year.

items.statement: A filter on a column of the grouped table belongs in the WHERE clause, not in a set-difference against the unfiltered rows.
items.when: The question restricts the counted set by a value of a column on the primary table while also requiring a HAVING condition on a joined table.

items.statement: Joining races to circuits on circuitId and filtering by circuit name yields one row per race, so duplicate attribute values appear when several races share that attribute.
items.when: The query joins races to circuits and selects a race attribute that is not unique per race.

items.statement: A query that returns a race attribute for races held at a named circuit must return distinct values when the question asks for the set of times rather than one row per race.
items.when: The question asks to list a race attribute for races held at a named circuit and the attribute can repeat across multiple races.

items.statement: A query that filters a child table and returns a parent identifier projects the foreign-key column directly, without DISTINCT, when the question asks which parents satisfy the condition.

items.statement: Adding DISTINCT to a projection of a foreign-key column that is not unique in the source table silently drops rows that belong to different parent records.
items.when: The question asks for parent IDs reachable through a child table whose join key is not unique per parent, and the projection contains only that key.

items.statement: A question phrased as 'top N teams with the highest X' orders the result by X descending, while 'lowest' or 'bottom' phrasing orders ascending.

items.statement: A question asking only for a measured attribute of the top-N teams returns that attribute column alone, without the team name column.
items.when: The question asks for a single measured attribute of the top-N teams and does not ask for team names.

items.statement: Joining a parent table to a child table without DISTINCT returns duplicate values of the parent's attribute when the parent has multiple children.
items.when: The selected column belongs to the table on the one side of a one-to-many join.

items.statement: A query that returns a single attribute from a table joined to another table must use DISTINCT when the join can produce multiple matching rows for one value of that attribute.
items.when: The question asks for one attribute of an entity that is joined to a table with a many-to-one or one-to-many relationship to it.

items.statement: The SELECT list must include every derived column the question asks for, including computed rank columns, in addition to the base columns being ranked.
items.when: The question requests a computed or derived value alongside base columns.

items.statement: A question that asks to rank rows requires a window function such as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ...) in the SELECT list, not merely an ORDER BY clause.
items.when: The question contains a ranking verb (e.g. 'rank') applied to a column.

items.statement: Rulings are joined to cards by matching cards.uuid to rulings.uuid.
items.when: The question involves rulings for a card identified by name or number.

items.statement: A query that asks to describe information about rulings for a card returns only the ruling text column, not the ruling date.
items.when: The question asks for information about rulings for a specific card identified by name and number.

items.statement: Joining Player to Player_Attributes on player_api_id produces rows whose values differ from the correct join on id.
items.when: The query joins Player and Player_Attributes and the join predicate references player_api_id.

items.statement: Joins between Player and Player_Attributes must match on the shared id column, not on player_api_id.
items.when: The query joins the Player and Player_Attributes tables.

items.statement: Joining races to circuits and filtering by country without DISTINCT can return duplicate race names when a race is associated with multiple matching circuit rows.

items.statement: A query that returns race names for circuits in a given country must return each race name at most once, so DISTINCT is required when the join can produce duplicate race rows.

items.statement: A query that ranks rows by an aggregate count should order by the count of the join key that links the two tables, not by a different column from the joined table.

items.statement: When a query groups by a column and also selects other columns from the same table, every selected non-aggregated column must appear in the GROUP BY clause.
items.when: The query uses GROUP BY with a mix of aggregated and non-aggregated selected columns.

items.statement: A count of races is computed over races.raceId, not over an unqualified COUNT(*).
items.when: The question asks how many races satisfy a condition.

items.statement: Country filters on the circuits table must list individual country names rather than continent names, because the country column stores countries.
items.when: The question asks to exclude or include races by geographic region such as Asia or Europe.

items.statement: A percentage numerator and denominator must both be computed over the same DISTINCT key set so the ratio is bounded by 100.
items.when: The query computes a percentage as a ratio of two aggregates over a joined result.

items.statement: Joining district on client.district_id and filtering district.A11 to its maximum does not identify the youngest client and can yield zero rows.

items.statement: When a date column stores year and month as a six-character string, filtering to a single year uses a prefix match on the first four characters rather than a BETWEEN range over month values.

items.statement: A query that counts groups satisfying a HAVING condition must wrap the grouped query in a subquery and count its rows, because COUNT with GROUP BY returns one row per group rather than a single total.
items.when: The question asks how many entities satisfy an aggregate condition over grouped rows.

items.statement: Joining circuits to races to results to constructors yields circuit rows rather than the standings positions a position question asks for.
items.when: The question asks for positions rather than circuit names, locations, or countries.

items.statement: Questions asking for positions associated with a constructor are answered from constructorStandings joined to constructors on constructorId, not from circuits or results.
items.when: The question asks for positions and names a constructor.

items.statement: In the card_games schema, the column holding a card's type is named `type`, not `types`.
items.when: The query filters cards by their card type.

items.statement: A query that projects a non-key column from a joined table while filtering on a one-to-many relationship must use DISTINCT to avoid duplicate rows.
items.when: The question asks for a single attribute value (a status, name, or category) rather than a count or aggregate, and the join can produce multiple matching rows per entity.

items.statement: When the question asks for the oldest female client's district, the district is selected by ordering clients with gender 'F' by birth_date ascending and taking the first, rather than by ordering the joined result rows.
items.when: The question asks for accounts of the oldest female client and the query joins client to district.

items.statement: A gap between a district's average salary and the maximum average salary across all districts is computed as the global MAX(A11) minus the global MIN(A11), not as MAX(A11) minus the selected district's A11.
items.when: The question asks for the gap between the lowest average salary and the highest average salary across districts.

items.statement: A query whose question asks which entity ranks highest returns exactly one row when a LIMIT 1 is applied.
items.when: The question asks for the single top-ranked entity and the query uses ORDER BY with LIMIT 1.

items.statement: A query that asks which entity ranks highest returns only the identifying column of that entity, not the aggregate used for ranking.
items.when: The question asks which customer, product, or other entity has the greatest or least value of some measure.

items.statement: Joining Player to Player_Attributes is unnecessary when the requested id and the ordering attribute both reside in Player_Attributes.
items.when: The question asks for an id and an ordering attribute that are both columns of Player_Attributes.

items.statement: When a question asks for a player id and the ranking attribute lives in Player_Attributes, the id column is Player_Attributes.id rather than Player.player_api_id.
items.when: The question requests a player id and the ordering attribute is a column of Player_Attributes.

items.statement: Joining races to circuits and filtering on circuit country without DISTINCT can return duplicate race names when a race is associated with multiple matching circuit rows.
items.when: The question asks for race names and the filter is on a circuit column rather than a race column.

items.statement: A query that asks for the name of a race held on circuits in a country must return each race name at most once, so DISTINCT is required when the join can multiply rows.
items.when: The question asks for race names filtered by a circuit attribute such as country.

items.statement: A filter on a column of one table must reference that table's alias, not another joined table's alias.
items.when: The query joins two tables and a WHERE predicate names a column that exists in only one of them.

items.statement: Applying DISTINCT to a column that is not unique per entity in the joined result can drop rows that belong to distinct entities sharing that value.
items.when: The question asks for a list of attribute values and the selected attribute may repeat across distinct matching entities.

items.statement: A ratio expression must not be wrapped in a CAST to REAL when the numerator already uses a decimal literal such as 1.0 to force floating-point division.
items.when: The SQL computes a ratio using SUM(CASE ...) over two groups.

items.statement: When a question asks for a ratio of A to B, the numerator must count A and the denominator must count B in the order named by the question.
items.when: The question asks for a ratio of one named group to another named group.

items.statement: When a query groups by a unique id plus a display column but selects only the display column, grouping by the display column alone yields the deduplicated result.

items.statement: Grouping by a unique identifier column in addition to the selected display column can produce duplicate display values when the identifier is not selected.
items.when: The query groups by both a unique id column and a name column while selecting only the name.

items.statement: Numeric-looking literal values are compared to numeric columns without surrounding quotes.

items.statement: A question that asks to name entities is answered by selecting the entity identifier column rather than a descriptive name column.
items.when: The question uses a naming verb such as 'name' and the target table has both an identifier column and a descriptive name column.

items.statement: When a question asks for an average count of bonds per molecule, the denominator is the number of molecules in scope, not the number of atoms.

items.statement: A question asking for an average per entity requires computing a per-entity aggregate in a subquery and then averaging those per-entity values, rather than dividing a global sum by a global count.

items.statement: Filtering a department column with a value that omits the stored suffix returns no rows.

items.statement: Date comparisons on a datetime column are wrapped with date() on the column side when the filter literal is a bare date.
items.when: The filter compares a datetime-typed column against a date literal without a time component.

items.statement: Counting questions over a table are answered with COUNT applied to a specific column of that table rather than COUNT(*).
items.when: The question asks how many rows or entities exist and the answer is a single count over one table.

items.statement: A WHERE column = (SELECT MAX(column) ...) pattern returns multiple rows when the maximum value is shared, so it does not satisfy questions that ask for a single top-ranked item.
items.when: The question requests one item and the target column may contain duplicate maximum values.

items.statement: Questions asking for the single card with the highest value of a numeric column require a query that returns exactly one row, such as ORDER BY that column DESC with LIMIT 1, rather than a WHERE equality against a MAX subquery that can match ties.
items.when: The question asks for one card name associated with the maximum of a numeric column.

items.statement: A subquery that computes per-molecule counts and is then averaged must group by molecule_id and expose a single count column for the outer AVG.
items.when: The question asks for an average of a per-entity count rather than a count of rows.

items.statement: When counting atoms of a given element per molecule, joining atom and bond directly on molecule_id and filtering bond_type in the WHERE clause yields the same per-molecule counts as joining through the molecule table.
items.when: The question asks for an average or aggregate over per-molecule counts of atoms of a specific element, and the schema links atom and bond via molecule_id.

items.statement: Returning one row per candidate value with ORDER BY and LIMIT 1 answers a ranking question, not a which-is-higher question.
items.when: the question asks which of two values is higher and the answer must name one of them

items.statement: Questions asking which of two values is higher require a single comparison result rather than a row per candidate value.
